base_properties.human_readable: Crown Cession Reading of Treaty Authority
base_properties.topic_domain: constitutional law / indigenous rights / colonial history

stakeholders.name: crown_government
stakeholders.situation: Claims exclusive sovereignty and legislative supremacy derived from the English treaty text; administers land alienation, courts, and enforcement apparatus.

stakeholders.name: settler_population
stakeholders.situation: Receives secure land titles and representative institutions under the Crown's legal framework; depends on the Crown's reading to validate their property claims against customary tenure.

stakeholders.name: maori_rangatira
stakeholders.situation: Held customary authority over land and people; under the Crown cession reading their signatory understanding is overridden by the English text, and their political authority is rendered subordinate or legally void.

stakeholders.name: maori_communities
stakeholders.situation: Lose land and customary resource access as the Crown's reading legitimizes large-scale alienation; excluded from English-law property rights unless individually granted.

stakeholders.name: maori_text_drafters
stakeholders.situation: Henry Williams and missionaries who drafted the MÄori text; their translation choices and assurances to chiefs are overridden by the English-text supremacy claim, and their voices are absent from the authoritative interpretive framework.

stakeholders.name: waitangi_tribunal
stakeholders.situation: Investigates treaty breaches and produces findings on MÄori text meaning; lacks power to override Crown sovereignty but provides external analytical assessment of the cession reading's historical validity.

six_questions.coordination_function: Establishes a single unified legal authority and land-title system over the territory, eliminating competing customary claims and providing governance certainty for the colonial project.
six_questions.transfer_function: Transfers sovereignty and legislative authority from MÄori customary structures to the Crown; transfers land from MÄori communal tenure to Crown-granted or alienated individual title, validated by the English text.
six_questions.absent_voices: MÄori signatories who understood kÄwanatanga as limited governance; MÄori text drafters whose translation was overridden; contemporary MÄori political movements asserting tino rangatiratanga as unextinguished.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: If the Crown cession reading vanished, the legal foundation for Crown sovereignty, parliamentary supremacy, and the bulk of derived land titles would be destabilized; the constitutional order would require renegotiation or replacement.
six_questions.founding_problem: Colonial administration required legal certainty over sovereignty and land tenure to enable mass settlement and govern territory acquired through treaty.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: British Colonial Office correspondence corroborates the 19th-century settlement imperative. Waitangi Tribunal historians and MÄori scholars corroborate that the problem was addressed through unilateral imposition rather than genuine cession; no impartial contemporary party attests the founding problem as uncontestedly live.

commentary.narrative_context: This constraint instantiates the Crown cession reading of the treaty authority cession kernel: the English text of the Treaty of Waitangi controls, kÄwanatanga is read as full sovereignty, and the treaty completes a legal cession of authority to the Crown. Structurally, this reading constructs a wall enclosing land and legislative authority under the Crown, extinguishing or subordinating MÄori customary authority and legitimizing land alienation. It is authored as one reading among siblings (rangatiratanga_retention_reading, biculturalism_reading, retrospective_snare_exposure) and carries the kernel's committer structure in cs_structure.

settler_population: Primary beneficiary (organized/constrained) â gains land titles and legal certainty
maori_rangatira: Primary payer (organized/trapped) â customary authority subordinated
maori_communities: Secondary payer (powerless/trapped) â land and resources alienated
maori_text_drafters: Excluded voice (moderate/trapped) â translation overridden

commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.82) is high because the reading enabled massive transfer of land and sovereignty with minimal reciprocity; suppression (0.88) is higher because persistence required military confiscation, the Native Land Court, and statutory bars on customary title. Accessibility_collapse (0.85) reflects near-total judicial and statutory extinguishment of MÄori legal alternatives by the mid-20th century. Resistance (0.75) captures the Waikato wars, Kingitanga, and modern treaty claims. Theater_ratio (0.30) is moderate-low: the legal machinery was functionally effective at extraction, though modern partnership rhetoric adds performative overlay.
commentary.perspectival_gap: From the Crown seat the reading is legitimate constitutional lineage and necessary order; from MÄori payer seats it is unilateral imposition using a mistranslated text. The engine computes this divergence from structural data: Crown has institutional power, arbitrage exit, and beneficiary role (d near 0.0); MÄori communities have powerless status, trapped exit, and payer role (d near 1.0). Settlers sit between, constrained by their dependence on Crown title but benefiting from the transfer.
commentary.directionality_logic: The Crown and settler population are structural beneficiaries: the Crown gains sovereignty and legislative supremacy, settlers gain secure property. Directionality is near the beneficiary end for the Crown (institutional/arbitrage) and moderate-low for settlers (organized/constrained). MÄori rangatira and communities are structural targets: they bear the loss of authority and land, with trapped exit options amplifying effective extraction. The Waitangi Tribunal observer seat is analytical with no directional extraction.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding problem â colonial legal order for settlement â is contested as to whether it persists or has been superseded by a different constitutional order. The Crown cession reading persists despite substantial authority erosion because dismantling it would rearrange the land-title system and sovereignty framework; the cost of genuine restoration exceeds what the Crown has been willing to bear, suggesting mandatrophy risk, though the reading is actively maintained rather than purely inertial.

omegas.question: Does the Crown cession reading validly derive sovereignty from a treaty text that MÄori signatories did not read or assent to in English?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Historical-linguistic analysis of the Williams translation and testimony from 1840; legal recognition of contra proferentem in treaty interpretation.
omegas.impact: If the MÄori text did not convey sovereignty cession, the Crown cession reading rests on a consent gap that transforms the constraint from a cession mechanism into a unilateral imposition.
omegas.description: Whether MÄori signatories consented to English-text sovereignty.

omegas.question: Can the colonial legal order's coordination function for settlers be separated from its extraction function directed at MÄori?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative analysis of jurisdictions where parallel MÄori customary title recognition was maintained alongside Crown sovereignty.
omegas.impact: If separable, the constraint is a tangled rope with distinct coordination and extraction strands; if inseparable, the coordination is the extraction mechanism itself.
omegas.description: Separability of coordination and extraction in the Crown cession reading.

omegas.question: Which reading of the treaty authority cession kernel does the current legal system structurally enforce?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Tracking which reading controls land-title determination, legislative supremacy claims, and constitutional recognition.
omegas.impact: If the Crown cession reading remains operationally dominant despite rhetorical partnership, extraction is ongoing; if superseded by partnership readings, the constraint becomes historical.
omegas.description: Operational dominance of the Crown cession reading versus sibling readings.
